newsitem.title: UK: CYCLING-TAFI STEPS UP WORLD CUP CHALLENGE.
newsitem.headline: CYCLING-TAFI STEPS UP WORLD CUP CHALLENGE.

text.p: Andrea Tafi stepped up his World Cup challenge with Italy's sixth triumph in eight visits to the British round on Sunday.
He finished 43 seconds clear as Andrea Ferrigato and Gianluca Bortolami completed a clean sweep for Italy in the 242 kms Rochester Classic.

His solo over the final 15 kilometres gave Tafi a boost of 100 points in the standings, which following his second placing in the Dutch round lifted him to third overall and 35 points behind series leader Rolf Sorensen of Denmark.

The Dane improved his lead to 29 points over Italian Michele Bartoli with 13th place, a minute behind Tafi whose biggest triumph until Sunday was winning the Giro di Lombardy World Cup round last year.
"Bortolami was my biggest fear. He has such great form," said Tafi who had escaped with Bortolami, the 1994 World Cup winner, and four others after 164 kilometres.
"When I heard that our lead was only 25 seconds I attacked to keep the group going, but I saved my real attack for the finishing circuit," Tafi added.
After two wins in the Tour of Malaysia, Tafi's season fell into the doldrums. "My team kept faith with me however. Now I am in good shape and looking forward to Zurich."

Zurich is the venue for next Sunday's eighth round, the Grand Prix OF Switzerland. Tafi is his team's new hope with Belgian team mate Johan Museeuw's quest to keep the Cup for a third year having faded.

Only 85 of the 140 starters completed the course, and among the non-finishers was Britain's Chris Boardman who injured his back in a fall. The world track champion is still recovering from a crash which forced him out of last month's Tour de France.
